events.title: Saturday Morning Physics | The Physics of Art and the Art of Physics
events.summary: Explore the intersection of physics and art in this hybrid lecture. Discover how scientific principles influence artistic creation and how beauty guides scientific discovery, featuring insights from a U-M Physics and Engineering professor.
events.imageAlt: Saturday Morning Physics | The Physics of Art and the Art of Physics
events.experienceId: experience:["ann arbor","weiser hall","saturday morning physics the physics of art and the art of physics"]

evidence.description: Moving from light and color through Helmholtz’s science of perception, this talk traces the remarkable journey from physical reality to what the eye sees, what the artist creates, and what the audience imagines—while discussing the physics principles behind it. It then turns the lens around to ask how beauty, elegance, and symmetry guide physicists in their search for the laws of nature.

events.title: Math Grad Show and Tell Seminar: A mathematical introduction to knitting
events.summary: Explore the mathematical underpinnings of knitting in this engaging seminar. Learn how knitted fabrics are constructed, delve into topological models, and discover a new stitch designed by physicists. Participants can even practice knitting a few stitches.
events.imageAlt: Math Grad Show and Tell Seminar: A mathematical introduction to knitting
events.experienceId: experience:["ann arbor","east hall","math grad show and tell seminar a mathematical introduction to knitting"]

evidence.description: In this talk, we will learn how knitted textiles are constructed and explore topological models of knitting. We will learn what it means to be knittable and meet a new knitted stitch that physicists designed to be less prone to unraveling than standard knitting. You will also get to practice knitting a few stitches for yourself!

events.summary: Experience an all-American program by Duo Dolce, featuring cello and piano works by composers like Gershwin, Beach, and Copland. This concert celebrates diverse cultural heritage and musical traditions, reflecting the country's rich mosaic of voices.
events.imageAlt: Kristen Yeon-Ji Yun, cello & Phoenix Park-Kim, piano

evidence.description: Duo Dolce presents an all-American program celebrating 250 years of American music, featuring works by composers including George Gershwin, Amy Beach, and Aaron Copland, alongside music shaped by immigrant and multicultural experiences. Together, these works create an American mosaic that reflects the country’s diverse cultural heritage, voices, and musical traditions.

events.title: Riders in the Sky
events.summary: Experience the legendary Riders in the Sky as they bring their award-winning harmonies, Western wit, and high-yodeling adventures to The Ark. This iconic group celebrates the heritage of Western music with both classic and original tunes.

evidence.description: What began as a celebration of classic Western Music and an evening of hilarity has become a career, and that career has become a legend, one which, 40 years on, shows no signs of stopping or even slowing down much.
